note: Fresh held-out set, written after the r2 fixes and labelled before it was run. Not used to tune. Labels are a designer's call, not the code's rule: shouldAsk is true when the request fits a part and a designer would ask before building (two shapes named, a nav with no platform, a data view with no state named). Buttons, CTAs, fields and state parts are labelled no-ask. expect is the part a designer means, or null when nothing in the Acme library fits. Part recall: fitting requests where brief offered expect (candidate, option, or candidate after the first option of each question). Part precision: requests where brief offered parts and expect was among them. Question recall and precision use shouldAsk. The numbers below are what the test measured; the test fails if they move. First run: question recall 9/12, precision 9/14; it found one bug (an approved decision matched on the part's own plural, so data tables of payments skipped as a decision), fixed before these numbers. Misses left: a nav bar for the app and top nav for the payees get no part because recommend finds none with the extra words (recommend recall, PR #59); fields, CTAs and buttons get a states question a designer would skip.
